models_evaluated: primary LLM-based medication safety review system
range of state-of-the-art LLMs and configurations

links.outcome: Whether LLM medication review correct in real-world NHS data beyond benchmark performance
links.effect: Sensitivity 100% and specificity 83.1% for recognising issues, but all issues and interventions correctly identified in only 46.9% [95% CI 41.1-52.8] of patients.
links.quote: Our primary LLM system showed strong performance in recognising when a clinical issue is present (sensitivity 100\% [95\% CI 98.2--100], specificity 83.1\% [95\% CI 72.7--90.1]), yet correctly identified all issues and interventions in only 46.9\% [95\% CI 41.1--52.8] of patients.

links.outcome: Persistence of failure patterns across patient demographic strata
links.effect: Failure patterns persisted across patient complexity and demographic strata, i.e., no subgroup was spared; not a subgroup-specific disparity.
links.quote: These patterns persisted across patient complexity and demographic strata, and across a range of state-of-the-art models and configurations.

links.outcome: LLM overconfidence under uncertainty in medication safety review
links.effect: Overconfidence in uncertainty was identified as one of five primary failure patterns.
links.quote: Failure analysis reveals that, in this setting, the dominant failure mechanism is contextual reasoning rather than missing medication knowledge, with five primary patterns: overconfidence in uncertainty, applying standard guidelines without adjusting for patient context, misunderstanding how healthcare is delivered in practice, factual errors, and process blindness.

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation of an LLM medication safety review system on real EHR data with detailed failure analysis, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
